target.title: fix(session-maintenance): preserve zero-valued fields in warning dedupe key
target.body:
Closes #99983

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose session-maintenance warning had a `pruneAfterMs` or `maxEntries` value of `0` would stop receiving re-warnings after limits changed. The dedupe key silently dropped zero-valued numeric fields, causing structurally different warning contexts to collide on the same key and suppress subsequent deliveries.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildWarningContext` assembled its dedupe key with `.filter(Boolean)`, which collapses falsy values including the number `0`. When `pruneAfterMs` or `maxEntries` was `0`, that slot was omitted, making two distinct warning contexts produce the same string. The fix wraps both numeric fields in `String()` and removes `.filter(Boolean)` so all five positional slots are always present in the key regardless of value.

## User Impact

Users with a `pruneAfterMs: 0` or `maxEntries: 0` session-maintenance limit will now correctly receive a new warning whenever that limit changes. Previously, changing from a non-zero limit to `0` (or between any configurations that included a zero-valued field) could silently suppress the re-warning.

## Evidence

### Test run — all 6 tests pass including new regression test

```
 RUN  v4.1.8 C:/tmp/openclaw-work

stderr | src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > enqueues a system event when outbound delivery fails
[session-maintenance-warning] Failed to deliver session maintenance warning: Error: boom

 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > forwards session context to outbound delivery 236ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > suppresses duplicate warning contexts for the same session 1ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > preserves zero-valued warning fields in the dedupe context 0ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > falls back to a system event when the last target is not deliverable 0ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > skips warning delivery in test mode 0ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > enqueues a system event when outbound delivery fails 77ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
   Start at  00:07:02
   Duration  1.33s (transform 988ms, setup 721ms, import 21ms, tests 361ms, environment 0ms)

EXIT:0
```

The regression test `preserves zero-valued warning fields in the dedupe context` directly exercises the fixed path: a warning with `pruneAfterMs: 0` now encodes as `${sessionKey}|0|10|prune|` instead of being collapsed by `.filter(Boolean)`.

### Key behavior verified by regression test

Before the fix, `buildWarningContext` would produce identical keys for these two structurally different warnings:
- `pruneAfterMs: 0, maxEntries: 10` → key: `${sessionKey}|10|prune|` (0 dropped)
- `pruneAfterMs: 5000, maxEntries: 10` → key: `${sessionKey}|5000|10|prune|`

After the fix, both produce distinct positional keys:
- `pruneAfterMs: 0, maxEntries: 10` → key: `${sessionKey}|0|10|prune|`
- `pruneAfterMs: 5000, maxEntries: 10` → key: `${sessionKey}|5000|10|prune|`

### Migration / stored-state note

This change affects only the in-process dedupe key computed at runtime from the current session config. The key is never persisted to disk or SQLite — it is held only in the per-session in-memory `Map`. On restart the map is empty, so there is no migration or upgrade compatibility concern.
